question.text: The requirement for research entities to maintain a functional website with specified details serves which investor protection purpose?

answer.text: It allows SEBI to track the entity's advertising expenditure

It gives investors easy access to SEBI-specified details — the RA's registered name, registration number, address and contact information, the required disclaimer, the Investor Charter, complaint data and links to SCORES and grievance channels
It serves only as a marketing tool for the research entity
It is required only for entities with more than 50 clients

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires a functional website carrying SEBI-specified details: the registered RA name, registration number, address and contact details, the prescribed disclaimer, the Investor Charter, complaint disclosures and complaint data, and access to SCORES / grievance redressal links. The Trap: The website rule is not about ad-spend tracking, marketing alone, or entity size; it exists so investors can verify and contact the RA and see complaint information in one place. Note: Broader client and material disclosure requirements (e.g., business activity, disciplinary history) are framed in the source as client disclosure, not as the full website-content rule, so keep those distinct.
